headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable, while pdf.js only processes PDFs with no network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list, so it does not ingest pdf.js outputs by default. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste of PDF-derived content into the list, which is an unusual configuration and limits blast radius. pdf.js can render PDFs, but no shared channel or parser is documented.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PDF text from pdf.js into awesome-selfhosted content fields, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted PDF text into curated entries.
Use a human review step before publishing list updates.
Disable any shared clipboard or sync tooling.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no network egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally and also has no network egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal documented, there is no clear leakage path beyond operator-mediated file transfer. The pair can still expose PDFs if the operator moves them between tools.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive PDFs into a shared directory accessible to both agents, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is connected to an external upload path not shown in the profiles, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Store PDFs in a separate folder from curated list content.
Use least-privilege file permissions on the workspace.
Delete temporary PDFs after processing.
Review outputs before copying them into the knowledge base.
requires-engineering: add access controls and audit logs for shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend with pdf.js over mutable resources. pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests, but without a shared writable directory, git state, or OAuth scope overlap, there is no documented write conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF both agents are later given write access to the same directory or repository, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free mutable state, reassess.
mitigations: Keep awesome-selfhosted read-only.
Run pdf.js in a separate temp directory.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Use file locks if shared outputs are introduced.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level coordination primitives.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge list, not an action-taking agent, so it does not automatically act on pdf.js outputs. pdf.js can produce rendered document content, but there is no documented pipeline where its output is treated as authoritative instructions by the list. The main risk is human or workflow error when transcribing PDF-derived facts into entries.
conditions: IF a workflow uses pdf.js output as the sole source for publishing list entries, cascading error risk increases.
IF an operator auto-imports extracted text without verification, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require manual verification of extracted facts.
Cross-check entries against original sources.
Use a checklist before publishing updates.
Separate extraction from curation roles.
requires-engineering: add citation validation for imported facts.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is documented for awesome-selfhosted, and pdf.js is only documented as handling PDF documents with no stated residency, retention, or regulated-data scope. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not evidenced, there is no specific mismatch to assess here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into pdf.js, reassess compliance obligations.
IF a deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here, the verdict may change.
mitigations: Avoid processing regulated PDFs in this pair.
Document data-handling boundaries.
Keep retention periods short.
Review vendor and hosting terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
